title: The Light Shines in the Darkness
speaker: Ryan Baird
summary: Satan got rope-a-doped. He threw everything he had at Jesus on the cross, and Jesus rose with the enemy spent. We win the way Jesus won.
exhortation: In 1974 Muhammad Ali and George Foreman fought one of the greatest fights in boxing history, the Rumble in the Jungle. That fight gave us the most famous use of what we now call the rope-a-dope. Ali tired out his opponent by letting him think he was winning. He stayed on the ropes and let Foreman throw punch after punch. It worked. Foreman was exhausted, and in the eighth round Ali knocked him out.

Why bring this up? Because I want us to see the incarnation of Jesus from the enemy's perspective. "The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it." We can read that too quickly and miss it. Satan got rope-a-doped, big time. How did he fall for it? He knew the Scriptures, but he didn't really understand them. Jesus came in weakness, and what Satan knew was impossible suddenly seemed possible.

Nothing is more hateful to Satan than Jesus. I think that's why he fell: humble Jesus, always submitting to the Father, loving Jesus, showing affection for weak humans. He couldn't stand the humility, patience and love. He thought he could do better, and he was thrown out of heaven. And then here was Jesus in the flesh, in weakness. Satan was ecstatic. There was no way he wasn't going to take his best shot, and at the crucifixion he didn't pull a single punch. He gave everything he had. And when Jesus rose from the dead after absorbing every blow, Satan had nothing left. He was spent, and he got knocked out. To add insult to injury, he was beaten by everything he hated: humility, patience, meekness, selflessness and love.

So remember today that we worship the King, the champion, the undisputed heavyweight champion of the world, infinitely greater than any athlete who ever lived. He isn't done winning. He's coming back with the belt on, no one will be able to take it from him, and by his grace we will share in his victory.

Three quick points of application. First, we do have a real enemy. Satan isn't dead yet. He has been humiliated, and we are in his crosshairs. Second, we win the way Jesus won: through humility, patience, meekness, selflessness and love. We can't win by going our own way. Third, it is by his grace that we get to fight. When we're surprised by how fierce the battle is, remember that Jesus is sharing his glory with us. He is saying we get to be champions with him. That's why we can count it all joy to suffer for Jesus: we win along with him.
prayer: Lord, the whole arc of history tells your story. It all revolves around you. You are the champion. Thank you for your victory.
Thank you for your humility and love, for walking the path Satan looked at as foolish and beneath him. You came down and became a man, and you walked the path only you could walk. Thank you, Jesus.
